cohort: 3222 women delivered by cesarean section out of 22,998 women delivering at a major district hospital obstetric unit in the UK over four 12-month periods every 10 years from 1976 to 2006
finding: While median blood loss remained steady over the study periods, there was an increase in excess blood loss cases in the final study year compared to the previous two, possibly due to reduced oxytocin doses, and transfusion rates declined, likely due to concerns about infections from blood products.
mod_finding: This study observed trends in blood loss and transfusion rates at caesarean section and found no significant change in median blood loss over time.
